sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A09
Every sixteen and seventeen year old applicant must log at least forty hours of coached road training, mixing professional school lessons and home practice in any share. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A09
Adults of eighteen or more must get a learner permit and hold it at least ninety days before any road test. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A09
An adult permit holder drives only under teaching and beside a commercial or secondary school instructor or a qualified trainer of twenty plus, licensed with no suspension across four or more straight years before training. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A09
Adults never licensed in Connecticut and holding no valid out of state license must take the eight hour safe driving course and show its attendance certificate. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A09
Before testing, applicants must know proper speed, turning and driving lanes, right of way yielding, yellow light stopping, safe backing, and every style of parking including hills and curbs. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A09
Before moving the test car, follow directions, scan parked cars and people nearby, clear and defog glass and mirrors, and brake before shifting out of park. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A09
During the drive, shift and accelerate smoothly, reach road speed promptly, keep a fitting space cushion, and stop with smooth safe braking. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A09
Signal every proper turn and show hand signals too, watch traffic and walkers through each turn at a fitting speed, and stay alert with sound judgment throughout. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A09
Once the permit time and training stand met, book the road test appointment and find sites at ct.gov/dmv/offices. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A09
Arrive in a class fitting, mechanically safe car with valid registration and insurance papers, since an unlicensed driver may not drive there alone. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A09
A long term leased car qualifies only with insurance naming the car and the lease company registrant, and no unlicensed applicant may test in a rental. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A09
An unsafe test car cancels the evaluation and earns a free rescheduled appointment. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A09
Road test day needs the learner permit, the CS-1 eight hour course proof, an eighty four dollar license fee payable after passing, and any required medical clearance letter. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A09
Sixteen and seventeen year olds also prove driver training with a home training CS-1, a commercial school certificate, or a secondary school certificate. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]
FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A10
Teens also prove two parent teaching hours on under eighteen law and teen driving perils, taken inside the required eight hour program. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A10
The road test scores seat and mirror setup, equipment use, sign and signal response with courteous yielding, backing and parking, basic turns, warning light reading, and any extra maneuvers the inspector orders. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A10
Branch offices take cash, money orders, personal checks, debit and credit cards, and bank checks, all checks payable to DMV. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A10
Qualifiers leave with a temporary paper card while the permanent license card follows by mail within twenty days. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A10
Newly licensed sixteen and seventeen year olds carry no passengers for six months except a licensed instructor, a licensed parent or guardian, or one twenty plus person with four straight licensed years and no suspension in the prior four. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A10
In months seven through twelve the only new passengers allowed are immediate family members. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A10
Teens may not drive from eleven at night to five in the morning unless riding for a job, school, worship, medical need, or as an assigned Safe Ride driver. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A10
Active volunteer fire, ambulance and emergency medical members answering or returning from calls, plus assigned Safe Ride drivers, skip the passenger and curfew limits. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A10
Permit holders and licensed sixteen and seventeen year olds must never overload seatbelts, drive public passenger or vanpool vehicles, touch any phone or mobile device even hands free, or carry motorcycle passengers within six months of endorsement. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A10
Organ donor sign up happens at licensing or renewal, online, or by mail, needs an appointment with current license or ID in hand, costs nothing, but changing the choice later needs a duplicate credential with a thirty dollar fee. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A11
For adults of eighteen or more the donor registry counts as legal donation authorization, so tell family and read more at ct.gov/dmv [A11] [A10].
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]
FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A11
DMV offers voter registration or updates with every license transaction at any time, receipts and forwards the form, and a registrar confirmation should land in about three weeks, while an address change also moves the voter record unless declined. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]
FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A11
The limited license program serves drivers whose abilities changed since licensing and newcomers who now qualify, on physician reports and possibly an inspector road skills test. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]
FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A11
Stable monitored conditions may still allow driving, but affected applicants should call Driver Services at least four months early at (860) 263-5723. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]
FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A11
Health bars run higher for commercial licenses and for licenses covering taxis, delivery vans, buses and school buses. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]
FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A11
A limited license can restrict driving to daylight from a half hour before sunrise to a half hour after sunset, to corrective non telescopic lenses, to ordinary highways, to automatic gears, to dual mirror cars seeing two hundred feet back, or to special control cars. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]
FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A11
Disabled residents who might drive with adaptive gear can seek state training through the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services at (860) 424-4844. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]
